allocated_capacity_note: Supabase's MCP project APIs do not expose a queryable disk-quota/plan field for this project. This plan reuses the MAX_SAFE_DB_MB=4500 guard established and consistently applied since Sprint 7's branch loaders as the working capacity ceiling. At 2052 MB current usage, utilisation against that ceiling is 45.6% — well under the 85% stop threshold regardless of the true plan quota, since Supabase's smallest paid tiers start at 8GB and the branch is a child of a project already comfortably operating at this size.

growth_budget_check: 119 MB estimated < 200 MB budget — PASS. Projected branch size after Sprint 9: ~2052 + 119 = ~2171 MB, 48.2% of the assumed 4500 MB ceiling — well under the 85% stop threshold.
documented_reductions_vs_spec: Time-series sales: trailing 12 months (not spec's 36) — the existing branch-resident sales marts only carry trailing-12-month monthly grain per Sprint 7's own capacity decision; re-promoting a full 36-month monthly history was assessed as disproportionate for this sprint's combined new-mart footprint and is deferred.

Time-series sales: 2 dwelling types only (detached_house, apartment_unit) — the two types with real NSW-wide sample depth; townhouse/villa and other types have too few branch-resident monthly cells to be a meaningful time series yet (see Phase 3 reclassification report for post-reclass coverage).

Time-series rent/yield: latest ~8 quarters (not spec's 20) — keeps row count proportionate to the sales reduction above; full quarterly history remains available in the existing full-history rent/yield marts (mart.suburb_rent_quarterly etc.) for anyone querying directly, this new mart is a compact 'recent trend' view specifically.

Approvals time-series: reuses the existing single rolling-12m supply marts rather than duplicating a monthly series — approvals data on the branch is already curated to a single current point per geography (Sprint 4 decision), consistent with keeping this addition minimal.

stop_conditions_checked.decision: PROCEED — capacity is safe under the documented assumptions and reductions above.
